# Profile 28 w/ Data MDTs | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn-sr/profile-28-w-data-mdts.md)
.

Continuing on from the previous lab, configure the PEs to switchover to data MDTs immediately for any customer traffic. Use up to 20 MDTs per PE.

[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn-sr/profile-28-w-data-mdts#undefined)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn-sr/profile-28-w-data-mdts#undefined-1)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn-sr/profile-28-w-data-mdts#undefined-2)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn-sr/profile-28-w-data-mdts#ff221265-7b17-40c7-b4d4-16ebc27ebe71)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn-sr/profile-28-w-data-mdts#id-0d491aa0-371f-4ad8-9213-ee409a713aef)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Profile 28 and 29 also allow for Data MDTs. These use a type 3 route to advertise a S-PMSI route.

In our network, the receivers have already joined the SSM group (1.1.1.1, 232.1.1.1). This prompts the type 3 route from XR5, even though there is currently no traffic.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FJBaZFckwKQGgA8AeQsGs%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dc94c91c3-759f-48ed-81d0-5aa5c7e4fde9&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=a9e9daa6cb211439938616a577fcced3&sv=3)

Remember that the root PE must setup the p2mp tunnel. But how can XR5 know which PEs are interested in receiving traffic for a S-PMSI tunnel? It can’t simply assume that all PEs in total are interested, like it can with the default MDT.

The answer is that the route type 4 is used by the leaf PEs to signal interest in receiving the traffic advertised in the type 3 route. With SR-p2mp, the root needs to know which PEs are interested. It sets the “leaf-info-required” flag in the type 3 route.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FcuRRkXRZjZGH2ZqaDPZu%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Db33d60df-70d2-4f2a-9a72-af8eae780132&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=ed1a95e11dc34484cc53864b85d65121&sv=3)

0x01 means leaf info required:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FL8D8oQpbEB9Tktzfg1Wn%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D448c161f-5f10-4d27-995d-a6b69c002b5f&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=8216d80105b95642075bc5bddaa829b0&sv=3)

XR7 and XR8 are interested in receiving this traffic and see the leaf-info-required flag. So they source their own type 4 routes which simply mean that they are interested in receiving the traffic for the specified (S, G) on the S-PMSI tree.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F3BfpkNlCo9msKPnBKrYc%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Daffd073c-a3fe-4911-bcf5-9164387af7b2&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=8b42e3ba1bdb8854f9ee09ceed3cdca6&sv=3)

XR5 then requests the PCE to compute the S-PMSI tree rooted at itself with receivers XR7 and XR8. We can see that there are now two p2mp policies rooted at XR5.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FliQdOgOxJxN94AES9X6J%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D4e91260e-6c13-4303-9a77-08148671ad50&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=a14af8df5b085f10932f1fffd413ad6b&sv=3)

Just as we’ve seen when using mLDP and P-PIM in the core for multicast tree building, the data MDTs optimize traffic flow, as the traffic is only delivered to PEs that are interested in receiving the traffic.

We can see information about the local data MDTs using the following command on the root. Notice that you can see the leafs which have advertised interest in joining the S-PMSI using the type 4 route.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F6JbJ75eZx9b4FxxtsH6O%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D7ee51607-5a74-422c-ab3f-021dcbb3277c&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=bf2fde6ca740ea45f792f23e5be7a1c1&sv=3)

We can see remote data MDTs using the following commands on the egress PEs. The **remote** keyword is a way to know if the PE has joined the MDT. If the PE has joined, you will see a non-zero value under “VRF Routes Using Cache.” The **cache** keyword also shows data MDTs the PE has learned about via type 3 routes.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FFld6n69KZIvAlsihUutZ%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D6b0c9662-813b-451d-9ee4-8a1a70e1e0fd&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=7d5d1e93f0e574d458c3c71fbd9fc7eb&sv=3)

Note that color and FRR are enabled on the data MDTs separately. You can use the same syntax as you saw in the last lab:

However, if you want to use particular colors for certain (S, G) flows, and enable FRR on only specific (S, G) flows, you can use an RPL.

Copy

    #XR5-8
    multicast-routing

      address-family ipv4
       mdt data segment-routing mpls 20 immediate-switch

Copy

    multicast-routing
     vrf CUSTOMER
      address-family ipv4
       mdt data segment-routing mpls 20 color 10 fast-reroute lfa immediate-switch

Copy

    route-policy DATA_MDT_RPL
      if destination in (232.1.1.0/24) then
        set on-demand-color 10
        set fast-reroute lfa
      endif
    end-policy

    multicast-routing

      address-family ipv4

# PIM-BiDir for IPv6 | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-bidir-for-ipv6.md)
.

Load **multicast.init.cfg**

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:multicast.init.cfg
     
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:multicast.init.cfg
    commit replace
    y

Configure XR4 as the RP for all IPv6 multicast groups. Advertise the RP mapping using BSR. Use BiDir for these groups.

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-bidir-for-ipv6#fbf84b44-8ef7-4d25-9df9-0fbfb2a2977e)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-bidir-for-ipv6#id-7688d994-f023-4fc5-8744-a2b71748fe78)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

PIM-BiDir for IPv6 works the same way as IPv4. The DF election is used to ensure a loop free topology for upstream traffic that is unconditionally forwarded towards the RP.

To begin, we can confirm that we learn the RP mapping via BSR, and that XR4 identified as the RP in bidir mode. For IPv6 PIM, BiDir support is enabled by default on both IOS-XE and IOS-XR. The **BD** flag appears to mean BiDir.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F72GSseBqCOWW2tlzIyEo%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D699cc14f-d6a0-49c5-b9db-e2a905351d3a&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=f8ffb48a87b8090af47c450a025e97bc&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FeX7AlFvSYWyz6aEtUbJ8%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dd71e1ae8-04f5-4766-9183-d881ed81d1ba&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=289fd15b3e6039c4cc9d44b2e64b7341&sv=3)

To make this simpler, we will just join a group from R5’s loopback. This mimicks a host joining on a physical interface.

We see on the RP that the tree is built to the receiver and the outgoing interface is the link to XR1.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FPwGsoJOwgJvt412uCOMD%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D21588bb3-0e53-44ee-9df8-9d6bb895427f&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=f7a211c2f39620370b1d6a417720d3ad&sv=3)

Let’s now ping this group from R1:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FBIkB8W8C3Ki2ibzZaiE2%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D2b223b58-b0f7-411f-bba7-a37bbea66217&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=30fc85426c9bc1722486fa5cb762166d&sv=3)

At R7, the traffic is forwarded towards the BiDir RP unconditionally. Interestingly, we see no entries at all under **show ipv6 mroute** or **show ipv6 pim topology**. However, we can see the ff00::/8 BiDir entry using **show ipv6 mrib route**:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FxhCxuHnxUvlyD2oJ0GAh%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Da7b83b96-f7db-4bc4-87cd-bc184a0ed4a8&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=0c5cf5cc3a2118536df59649799f5101&sv=3)

R7 is accepting on all interfaces that are DF or upstream interfaces, and only forwarding out the upstream interface. Just like BiDir for IPv4, we can check the DF election results. R7 did not win the DF election with XR1, so this interface is not available as an incoming interface.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FlKEWseyMcMxsxLgfY8xH%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D548e02f4-2220-4cbc-b0d7-1bd9c7e79a0c&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=cbcbe0b73e39eedae324525d077d36c7&sv=3)

A similar command can be used on IOS-XR:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FjUufP4vNCf3M8BY0QXxv%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Df937abac-7907-4258-96dc-22470f9f57a6&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=c4c01e3417448c0c52bb8a8608d4becf&sv=3)

### A note on IPv6 PIM-SM with PIM-BiDir[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-bidir-for-ipv6#id-956de98f-94fe-4260-b750-5998c815c6f9)

For IPv4 on IOS-XE, we cannot use the same loopback for the RP for both PIM-SM and PIM-BIDIR. This is because the command overrides itself when you try to use the same loopback for two separate PIM RP commands.

This is again an issue for IPv6 when using BSR on IOS-XE.

However, it is not an issue when using static IPv6 RP assignment on IOS-XE:

Like we saw for IPv4 on IOS-XR, IPv6 on IOS-XR allows both commands for either BSR or static RP.

[PreviousPIM-BiDir](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-bidir)
[NextPIM-BiDir with Phantom RP](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-bidir-with-phantom-rp)

Last updated 1 year ago

*   [Answer](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-bidir-for-ipv6#fbf84b44-8ef7-4d25-9df9-0fbfb2a2977e)
    
*   [Explanation](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-bidir-for-ipv6#id-7688d994-f023-4fc5-8744-a2b71748fe78)
    
*   [A note on IPv6 PIM-SM with PIM-BiDir](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-bidir-for-ipv6#id-956de98f-94fe-4260-b750-5998c815c6f9)
    

Copy

    #XR4
    multicast-routing
     address-family ipv6
      interface Loopback0 enable
    !
    router pim
     address-family ipv6
      bsr candidate-bsr 2001::14
      bsr candidate-rp 2001::14 bidir

Copy

    #R5
    int lo0
     ipv6 mld join-group ff08::5

Copy

    ipv6 pim bsr candidate rp 2001::9 group-list PIM_SM_V6
    ipv6 pim bsr candidate rp 2001::9 group-list PIM_BIDIR_V6 bidir <---- This just replaces the previous command

Copy

    ipv6 pim rp-address 2001::7 PIM_SM_V6
    ipv6 pim rp-address 2001::7 PIM_BIDIR_V6 bidir  <--- Both commands are taken

Copy

    router pim
     address-family ipv6
      rp-address 2001::14 PIM_SM_V6
      rp-address 2001::14 PIM_BIDIR_V6 bidir
    !
    ! or
    !
    router pim
     address-family ipv6
      bsr candidate-rp 2001::14 group-list PIM_SM_V6 priority 192 interval 60
      bsr candidate-rp 2001::14 group-list PIM_BIDIR_V6 priority 192 interval 60 bidir

# Using IOS-XR as a Sender/Receiver | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/using-ios-xr-as-a-sender-receiver.md)
.

Load **ios-xr.mcast.host.init.cfg**

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:ios-xr.mcast.host.init.cfg
     
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:ios-xr.mcast.host.init.cfg
    commit replace
    y

XR3 is now a host. It does not run multicast or OSPF, and only has a default 0/0 route to R9.

On R2, join SSM group (11.9.13.13, 232.1.1.1) and (200b:11:9:13::13, FF35::1). Ping these groups from XR3 and ensure that it receives replies from R2.

On XR3, join SSM group (9.2.5.2, 232.1.2.3) and (2009:9:2:5::2, FF35::1). Ping this group from R2 and ensure that it receives replies from XR3.

You must enable IPv4 PIM SSM for this task.

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/using-ios-xr-as-a-sender-receiver#a9d1497d-27b0-4741-bd6a-dbed578abca8)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/using-ios-xr-as-a-sender-receiver#id-93cbde9b-d4c6-42a4-a8c7-6dcd4b4ac1e6)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When using IOS-XR as the sender, you must specify the interface. This appears to work as an outgoing interface keyword. On IOS-XE, the router appears to always send traffic out all interfaces, and the source address just specifies what source IP address to use. If you forget the source parameter on IOS-XR, the traffic will not be forwarded out any interface.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252Fx2iPFrV7p5wJ50vwhvD4%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dd007418f-3dca-4bf7-81f2-3f811cc7d46c&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=defbc97805b1a131c340c4af4e54d027&sv=3)

When using IOS-XR as the receiver, the router will not send an IGMP Join until you enable multicast on that interface. This is unlike CSR1000v, which _will_ send an IGMP Join with simply the **ip igmp join-group** command.

Pinging this group from R2 should result in replies from XR3.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FOlujt5EO2aQAD03ctwiK%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Ddcec1e91-f7cf-45ea-a2ad-aa23aa049e4f&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=b2d8c12500816a684bbd23500675827e&sv=3)

Similar to CSR1000v, the XRv router will enable PIM and create an entry for the group it has joined.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FLKm6pxLdJmaC5R3vm9h5%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D0bab4289-5ec9-4382-9d41-a76f353c93a8&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=3e7ad9c0a4328728328c931facd153e4&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252Fv4fZSRzug6KOELf3Qabk%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dc5d3ebe3-8e36-4302-8a08-49d9864b4de7&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=d6a75c3f6d504296b5ce17cbbd4eb5a9&sv=3)

When using IOS-XR as a sender for IPv6, you must enable multicast on the output interface. (You do not need to do this for IPv4). You also do not need to specify the outgoing interface, although it doesn’t hurt.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FDnND8sLJAOgy7bUcmg7E%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D472190f8-6796-4337-a37a-a5607f30fbe7&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=75cd4559a2b608ee5b56d9d5638a1e4e&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FRk6h5y07ZfV27WHJU867%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D36e7b175-439b-40dc-875f-fba3a5113892&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=f1aa58a5087a0b74f666116ad37c54c9&sv=3)

When using IOS-XR as a receiver for IPv6, you enable the interface for multicast address-family IPv6, and join the group under **router mld**. This is no different than using IOS-XR as a receiver for IPv4.

We can ping this group from R2 and receive replies from XR3:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F0hcwbxBsZ4ght3hT7PR2%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D48b9b89c-140d-44b1-8060-a7d4376797c6&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=e1ddd877ba02dce357166545f8b1b7a5&sv=3)

# Basic Interdomain Multicast w/o MSDP | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/basic-interdomain-multicast-w-o-msdp.md)
.

Load **inter-as.multicast.msdp.init.cfg**

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:inter-as.multicast.msdp.init.cfg
     
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:inter-as.multicast.msdp.init.cfg
    commit replace
    y

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252Fm3fEsJ3BKk4lsoOi3XMs%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3De69b990a-9995-4920-bc39-b8b7cdbec4bd&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=c1df37ca36d883397e2f5e5d3d92ee71&sv=3)

On R2, enable multicast, PIM, and join the group (\*, 239.1.1.1). On R4, send traffic to to 239.1.1.1. R4 should receive a reply from R2. Do not use MSDP to achieve this.

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/basic-interdomain-multicast-w-o-msdp#d46dc562-58cc-453b-bfe5-e36805695f41)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/basic-interdomain-multicast-w-o-msdp#a8934c35-9abd-41a8-a924-623cc6eb90a1)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Inter-domain multicast for ASM generally requires MSDP. However, this lab demonstrates an alternative to MSDP. By using the IGMP **static-group** command, the sending domain can forward the traffic out the interface to the receiving domain.

First, R2 joins group (\*, 239.1.1.1). R10 is the RP for this domain, so the RP tree is only built from R2 to R10.

Next, R4 starts sending, but R9 does not notify R10 of active sources, because they are not running MSDP. As a workaround, R9 can use **static-group** on the interface connecting to R6 to unconditionally forward the traffic out that interface.

R9 adds this interface to the OIL for (\*, 239.1.1.1):

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F0VWVcNMqH3XMO3hbFlpO%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Da2aaf9ec-6189-4ae0-a2ee-04dfe0229d1f&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=53567a65e34c960cbbecc5a98efc81eb&sv=3)

Next, R4 starts sending and R9 forwards the traffic to R6. However, R6 realizes that the traffic is not sourced from the directly connected subnet, so it does not Register the traffic with R10. Instead, we can run dense-mode on R6 and configure R6 to proxy a PIM Register for received traffic. This was originally a way to bridge together a dense-mode and sparse-mode domain, but this tool can also be used in this context to achieve basic inter-domain multicasting.

Now when R4 sends, R6 registers this with R10. R10 can now join the SPT (11.4.13.4, 239.1.1.1):

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F2ypnHT9mjq9wC3abVQWa%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D61beb9f4-1da8-4f3e-af40-a17d568ee687&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=1a9e87818b6bdc7f99d5687e934762fe&sv=3)

Traffic is now working:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FSo37md3QDPjuGZKbLHYo%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Df9b72e8a-dcf6-433f-805e-3194e60ebfe2&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=afc0a0f4ff8795ef91dbb98b6e064b3c&sv=3)

[PreviousRP Discovery Methods](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/rp-discovery-methods)
[NextBasic Interdomain Multicast w/ MSDP](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/basic-interdomain-multicast-w-msdp)

Last updated 1 year ago

*   [Answer](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/basic-interdomain-multicast-w-o-msdp#d46dc562-58cc-453b-bfe5-e36805695f41)
    
*   [Explanation](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/basic-interdomain-multicast-w-o-msdp#a8934c35-9abd-41a8-a924-623cc6eb90a1)
    

Copy

    #R2
    ip multicast-routing distributed
    !
    int Gi2.525
     ip pim sparse-mode
     ip igmp join-group 239.1.1.1
    
    #R9
    int GigabitEthernet2.569
     ip igmp static-group 239.1.1.1
    
    #R6
    int gi2.569
     ip pim dense-mode proxy-register list 100
    !
    ip access-list ext 100
     permit ip any any

Copy

    #R9
    int GigabitEthernet2.569
     ip igmp static-group 239.1.1.1

Copy

    #R6
    int gi2.569
     ip pim dense-mode proxy-register list 100
    !
    ip access-list ext 100
     permit ip any any

# PIM Boundaries with AutoRP | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-with-autorp.md)
.

Load **multicast.multi.domain.init.cfg**

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:multicast.multi.domain.init.cfg
     
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:multicast.multi.domain.init.cfg
    commit replace
    y

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FAkAV1xhPMuAstlt6rWUN%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D540a148d-26ce-462a-98cc-fbe099f5e166&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=bd34140c44184772f87f808726d9d7fe&sv=3)

Configure the group of routers circled on the left as a sub-PIM domain. R6 should be the RP for group range 239.10.0.0/24. This information should be propagated using AutoRP and should not leak outside this sub domain.

Configure R9 as the RP for group range 239.20.0.0/24 using AutoRP. This group range should be for domain-wide traffic, and should propagate to all routers in the topology.

Note that an interface has been added between R9 and XR2.

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-with-autorp#id-96513028-d94a-4a76-a6d2-7bde4407214d)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-with-autorp#a3d198ef-d20d-4c2a-a169-df6521b66685)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

PIM’s use of the underlying unicast topology makes PIM an overlay technology. The PIM domain is overlaid ontop of the unicast underlay. Routers also do not have the ability to run multiple PIM processes like they do for an IGP. This means that the PIM domain is essentially bounded by the collection of routers that share RP mapping information.

In some scenarios, you may want to create multiple PIM sub domains within a single IGP. The easiest way to do this is to limit the propagation of RP information to each sub domain.

In this lab, we have a sub domain that is circled on the left, yet we also want to create a topology-wide domain of all PIM routers. This makes it tricky to bound the sub domain’s RP advertisements.

To begin, we advertise RP mappings in AutoRP just like before. AutoRP actually lets us define the TTL of the C-RP and MA messages, but this is very rarely a good tool for bounding the domain. For example, on R6, if we make the TTL=2, R9 will still learn the mappings but R7 will not.

Next, we use the **multicast boundary** feature to prohibit the advertisement of the sub domain’s AutoRP mapping to router that don’t belong to the sub domain. On IOS-XE, we can actually filter the content of the AutoRP messages. Any mappings that are not permitted by the ACL are filtered out of the AutoRP message.

By using **debug ip pim auto-rp** we can watch that R6 is filtering the 239.10.0.0/24 mapping from Auto-RP messages sent in/out of Gi2.562 and Gi2.569:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FJdqr26E2YtkZA7abDu4c%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D8ad45435-4193-485f-aede-a43e87486f00&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=73705bc98b3baa6b0fdf304108c3bd5f&sv=3)

IOS-XR does not have this ability. Instead, all we can do is filter the Auto-RP RP-discovery packets entirely. In addition, IOS-XR denies the local multicast group 239.10.0.0/24. This prevents multicast traffic in this group range from using these interfaces, as this traffic should be bound to the local sub domain.

Note that if all we had was IOS-XR routers on the edge between the sub domain and the rest of the topology, we could not use AutoRP for disseminating RP information, as there would be no way to selectively permit the 239.20.0.0/24 RP mapping but deny 239.10.0.0/24.

We’ve also introduced another problem: Now R7 and XR4 are only receiving the 239.20.0.0/24 RP mapping information through XR1, which is not the shortest path. For this reason, the (R9, 224.0.1.40) traffic does not pass the RPF check (remember this is basic dense mode traffic). XR4’s route to R9 is via the direct link. And R7’s best route to R9 is via XR4.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F0jcND4IYmKOwlUMZeTHO%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Df5a7ce37-46b7-488c-8ced-4db915f0f4c4&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=0c9eeaeb7a4601cf31b906da5999cc3c&sv=3)

To fix this, we can increase the IGP cost of the links towards R9 via XR4-R9 link so that the RPF check will pass.

On all routers in the sub domain, we should see two RP mappings:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252Fxw4HqKcCN1vGZHHRvvBt%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D67b55137-9557-4d82-a348-60648f2a731b&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=c7907be077fa66df8a66f010491559b6&sv=3)

On a router that does not belong to the sub domain, we should only see an RP mapping for the 239.20.0.0/24 group range:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FJd5vfVyylygmnICkN3B1%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D532cbbb6-5f65-410c-9652-58e929b43964&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=37ac686aab0d175bf6d6e49dcd6c9584&sv=3)

### A note on AutoRP filtering[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-with-autorp#id-3dda006a-0475-4d36-b3b2-9acfd8af0d79)

When you apply the AutoRP filter, it appears to also work as a normal, data plane boundary. So you must ensure that the 224.0.1.40 group is permited through.

In this lab, we simply had a permit all statement:

However, if you use inverse logic, only permitting groups you want to pass the filter, you must ensure to add **permit host 224.0.1.40**.

[PreviousPIM Security](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-security)
[NextPIM Boundaries with BSR](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-with-bsr)

Last updated 1 year ago

*   [Answer](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-with-autorp#id-96513028-d94a-4a76-a6d2-7bde4407214d)
    
*   [Explanation](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-with-autorp#a3d198ef-d20d-4c2a-a169-df6521b66685)
    
*   [A note on AutoRP filtering](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-with-autorp#id-3dda006a-0475-4d36-b3b2-9acfd8af0d79)
    

Copy

    #R5-10
    ip pim autorp listen
    
    #R9
    int lo0
     ip pim sparse-mode
    !
    ip access-list standard DOMAIN_SCOPE_RANGE
     10 permit 239.20.0.0 0.0.0.255
    !
    ip pim send-rp-discovery lo0 scope 255
    ip pim send-rp-announce Loopback0 scope 255 group-list DOMAIN_SCOPE_RANGE
    
    #R6
    int lo0
     ip pim sparse-mode
    !
    ip access-list standard LOCAL_SCOPE_RANGE
     10 permit 239.10.0.0 0.0.0.255
    !
    ip pim send-rp-discovery lo0 scope 255
    ip pim send-rp-announce Loopback0 scope 255 group-list LOCAL_SCOPE_RANGE
    !
    access-l 1 deny 239.10.0.0 0.0.0.255
    access-l 1 permit any
    !
    int GigabitEthernet2.562
     ip multicast boundary 1 filter-autorp
    int GigabitEthernet2.569
     ip multicast boundary 1 filter-autorp
    
    #XR4
    ipv4 access-list BOUNDARY_ACL
     10 deny ipv4 239.10.0.0/24 any
     20 deny ipv4 host 224.0.1.40 any
     30 permit ipv4 any any
    !
    multicast-routing
     address-family ipv4
      interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0.524
       boundary BOUNDARY_ACL
      !
      interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0.594
       boundary BOUNDARY_ACL
    !
    router ospf 1
     area 0
      interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0.524
       cost 100
      !
      interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0.594
       cost 100
    
    #R7
    int GigabitEthernet2.574
     ip ospf cost 100

Copy

# PIM-SM with BSR for IPv6 | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-with-bsr-for-ipv6.md)
.

Load **multicast.init.cfg**

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:multicast.init.cfg
     
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:multicast.init.cfg
    commit replace
    y

*   Configure R9 and XR4 as RPs for all IPv6 groups using BSR.
    
    *   Both R9 and XR4 should be BSRs as well.
        
    *   R9 should be the preferred BSR and Candidate RP.
        
    

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-with-bsr-for-ipv6#id-08b045e9-e80a-4102-8d6e-f8a7995ab72f)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-with-bsr-for-ipv6#d0f3a097-9a9e-4652-a13b-6d743b57ee11)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

BSR for IPv6 works very much the same as BSR for IPv4. There is a minor difference with the default priority values for IOS-XE, though. IOS-XE conforms to the RFC standard and uses priority 192 for the C-RP advertisement.

Just like for IPv4 BSR, IOS-XE uses a default BSR priority value of 0, and IOS-XE uses a default BSR priority value of 1. For this reason, we specify priority value 2 on R9 so that it will be the elected BSR.

On R9 we can see that it has won the BSR election and that it has an RP-cache consisting of both 2001::9 and 2001::14 for ff00::/8.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FkNAQFaXugkDj9kXgy6aV%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Da8dcfd96-5866-47a0-90e9-0ded1ee2bf22&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=7b37176cfe43cf7cffc607bc5ad14ac3&sv=3)

On any other router, the “show ipv6 pim bsr rp-cache” command will show nothing. This is only useful on the BSR itself. However, we can see the IPv6 PIM RP mapping using the following command.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F87jWHTqWWNAS6y9dItcP%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dc362f872-b35f-4a52-9612-521f08dac0bb&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=2acac8cca0b9bb784dec0276cc48fd54&sv=3)

Using the command **show ipv6 pim group-map <group address>** we can see which RP wins the election. When the priories tie, the hash mask length is used just like with IPv4 BSR. We can see the hash mask length value using **show ipv6 pim bsr election**. This is 126 by default.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FEwqt51BMYEy2ab0jEkqE%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D89ee8648-1313-4ea2-9442-04284be62f05&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=7de3d4ab210aca3fe6dab65adfd736f1&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252Fv6R9iiYffXi9atUuZ86T%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dbf453ba4-ff93-43ef-b9ea-36549e630498&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=9855378446464f839d5463e553459637&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FDXJzyNeemNHozykBUymm%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D76cbdec2-ee10-4cb6-a259-49f3a819c344&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=19b75a0f03e6a4a9d98272a586b4b918&sv=3)

Strangely, I can never get 2001::14 to be used.

Similar commands can be used on IOS-XR. Interestingly, I can get XR3 to use XR4 as an RP for some groups. This appears to be a bug in IOS-XE.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FSvTuPEHPcZ2p1XKP3zSd%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D8b7ab804-93b8-4901-933a-6a0547e74bcb&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=ca21a5b8dfeb3798b55dc7f214d6a8e8&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F9G0zmZp48uFwB3iuk4gG%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D26347fd4-0357-4f19-8718-3ff5d56e7b6f&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=794590758a89c557df045bfcbdaea8aa&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FBJR4LGQ6isb6CXyx6YMg%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D7eb909b8-0fae-43fe-80e7-2b255bea56ad&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=e9a7bbbef95b3b9b7fc494f69b17e8bb&sv=3)

### Failover Considerations[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-with-bsr-for-ipv6#id-000cb627-9bd3-4bff-b1ad-bd39ac796018)

Failover does not appear to be as robust with IPv6 PIM. When I shutdown Lo0 on R9, I don’t see automatic failover on all other routers. In fact, R9 continues caching itself as C-RP in **show ipv6 pim bsr rp-cache** output. R9 stops sending BSR messages so its boot strap messages eventually time out on all other routers, and all routers are left with no RPs at all. Next, XR4 elects itself as BSR and floods its RP mapping with only itself as C-RP. Other downstream routers learn this. But there was a period of time when some routers had no RP information at all in my lab.

[PreviousPIM-SM with BSR](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-with-bsr)
[NextPIM-BiDir](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-bidir)

Last updated 1 year ago

*   [Answer](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-with-bsr-for-ipv6#id-08b045e9-e80a-4102-8d6e-f8a7995ab72f)
    
*   [Explanation](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-with-bsr-for-ipv6#d0f3a097-9a9e-4652-a13b-6d743b57ee11)
    
*   [Failover Considerations](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-with-bsr-for-ipv6#id-000cb627-9bd3-4bff-b1ad-bd39ac796018)
    

Copy

    #XR4
    multicast-routing
     address-family ipv6
      interface Loopback0 enable
    !
    router pim
     address-family ipv6
      bsr candidate-bsr 2001::14
      bsr candidate-rp 2001::14
    
    #R9
    ipv6 pim bsr candidate bsr 2001::9 priority 2
    ipv6 pim bsr candidate rp 2001::9

Copy

    #R9
    ipv6 pim bsr candidate bsr 2001::9 priority 2

# PIM-SM without Receiver IGMP Joins | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-without-receiver-igmp-joins.md)
.

Load **multicast.init.cfg**

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:multicast.init.cfg
     
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:multicast.init.cfg
    commit replace
    y

Receivers R2 and R4 cannot run IGMP. You’ve been asked to forward multicast traffic for (\*, 239.1.1.1) towards these receivers, despite their inability to signal interest in this group. Without using the command **ip igmp join-group** on any router, configure the LHRs to forward (\*, 239.1.1.1) traffic towards these receivers.

Configure R9 as the PIM-SM RP using BSR.

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-without-receiver-igmp-joins#id-82f212ee-5b08-4b34-86d7-36d7cb5af12e)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-without-receiver-igmp-joins#id-2346a70a-c643-4153-97d4-6cc6ff709e16)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The IGMP **static-group** command works the opposite as the **join-group** command. The **igmp join-group** command configures the router to act as a client and send an IGMP Report for the given group. The **static-group** command configures the router to act as if it received an IGMP Report on that interface. You are statically creating an IGMP group mapping for the given interface, without dynamically receiving an IGMP report from a client. This can be useful in situations for troubleshooting or if the clients do not have the ability to run IGMP.

On IOS-XE, we can see that the group has no expiration and the last reporter is 0.0.0.0. Additionally, there is an SG flag on the entry seen using the **detail** keyword.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FGS1FkQvoROkOiNUB6YJ4%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dc83485a9-3446-4819-b23a-be8d1c6c98e4&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=c97844da863192e1be04d417fb547ad8&sv=3)

On IOS-XR, the reporter is itself. It also has no expiration.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FQJEOIWwfWFEEGQGgFZ10%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D21d9b2ba-ae37-465a-9160-4b9c117fc5d3&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=b7d3f664c89b9e1734706acddb93bef5&sv=3)

The LHRs join the (\*, G) RPT the same as if this IGMP Report was received from a receiver. On R9 we see two interfaces in the OIL for the (\*, G) entry:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FoozHVKJY08M5CFakEtEb%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D003f6056-f482-4c0a-ade4-8b9ce914385a&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=aeec61735891648126d1e7ec0a7a8c58&sv=3)

If we source multicast traffic to this group address, we won’t get any ICMP replies, but we can verify that traffic is indeed being distributed to the LHRs and the LHRs are forwarding this out the interface to R2 and R4.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F8TO7Ey7e6gt8hXI7t1tP%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D701aca16-de0e-4a2f-ae30-d8905e07db4b&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=29c54b15bdbbf391718a78f86e63a912&sv=3)

On R5, we see 1 packets forwarded in “hardware” for the (\*, G) entry, and 13 forwarded for the (S, G) entry. Gi2.525 is in the OIL, so this confirms that the traffic was delivered to R2.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FYEbXA6RCVuuoV68yiT8c%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D2ad89725-06bd-4b44-acce-b976f6cb7ebc&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=2b227f08eee59642292d9974eb613807&sv=3)

We see similar output on XR3:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FKHr8J5dotR2TcQYXlODh%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Df1b3b9ff-26bc-490f-a41b-b5c333b90baf&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=40de8414b29a88442aef6c2210172ba4&sv=3)

### IPv6 MLD static-group[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-without-receiver-igmp-joins#f5d43f0d-6361-4728-bc5d-6075fe15e961)

This same idea works for MLD using the same **static-group** command.

The (\*, G) RP tree is created:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FVnGtg2B6Nla8PL70oe8A%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D180d22ef-7702-46df-aa66-0f30569f123f&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=126c849409c47818d39bdecf46e11a3f&sv=3)

Traffic sent towards this group is forwarded out the interfaces where the **mld static-group** command was configured.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FBgbpnCAliVJF79ftKj6l%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D36e92e85-9e50-497c-8f6b-8a3a958a3205&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=15dce0213dada041905ee477a9d9b1ff&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F7sr49yb8L7GRjzI3O2mN%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D50f1f2e6-3431-4017-ac68-2c9ce0a6a208&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=8803ff0b181abb8fd6f048f1280c01dc&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FGjv7cXK8HDPNfQ7AqMco%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D83b9c336-f15f-48ef-8a0b-1f7a98ad83b5&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=f814a55544fe987045edcc16b81ae83f&sv=3)

*   [Answer](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-without-receiver-igmp-joins#id-82f212ee-5b08-4b34-86d7-36d7cb5af12e)
    
*   [Explanation](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-without-receiver-igmp-joins#id-2346a70a-c643-4153-97d4-6cc6ff709e16)
    
*   [IPv6 MLD static-group](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-sm-without-receiver-igmp-joins#f5d43f0d-6361-4728-bc5d-6075fe15e961)
    

Copy

    #R9
    int lo0
     ip pim sparse-mode
    !
    ip pim bsr-candidate lo0
    ip pim rp-candidate lo0
    
    #R5
    int gi2.525
     ip igmp static-group 239.1.1.1
    
    #XR3
    router igmp
     int Gi0/0/0/0.543
      static-group 239.1.1.1

Copy

    #R9
    ipv6 pim bsr candidate bsr 2001::9
    ipv6 pim bsr candidate rp 2001::9
    
    #R5
    int gi2.525
     ipv6 mld static-group ff05::1
    
    #XR3
    router mld
     interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0.543
      static-group ff05::1

# Profile 21 | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-21.md)
.

Load **basic.startup.config.with.cpim.cfg**

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:basic.startup.config.with.cpim.cfg
    Y
    
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:basic.startup.config.with.cpim.cfg
    commit replace
    y

The basic IP addresses, L3VPN, and C-PIM between the PEs and CEs is pre-configured.

*   Configure multicast VPN using unicast ingress replication in the core.
    
*   You cannot use PIM or mLDP in the core.
    
*   Use BGP for auto-discovery of participating PEs.
    
*   Configure support for SSM in the C-PIM.
    
*   Use BGP as the overlay - PEs are not allowed to form C-PIM adjacencies with each other.
    

NOTE: Profile 21 is not in the v5.1 blueprint.

See answer below (scroll down).

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-21#id-99f0fcb0-73f3-42d2-93f2-f2d8cbbd09a2)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This is the same as profile 19, but we use BGP as the overlay instead of C-PIM.

Verification[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-21#id-0912d7a5-256e-4bf0-8f58-6b64932039a0)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

BSR again does not seem to be supported in the C-PIM. Instead I join a group on C2 again for (C1, G).

Verify that the PIM Join converts to a BGP route type 7:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FnDW4MGUxgaf9AYC8ExEk%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D339f9d5a-91fb-41ca-88be-d9a2272bedd9&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=bdb5f04dd13ad24f120198fa65bb71b0&sv=3)

These type 7 routes on PE1, received from PE2, are converted back into a PIM Join towards CE1 as we have seen before.

If desired, test S-PMSI as well. This works the same as we saw with profile 19 using type 3 and type 4 routes.

[PreviousProfile 19](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-19)
[NextMVPN SR](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn-sr)

Last updated 1 year ago

*   [Answer](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-21#id-99f0fcb0-73f3-42d2-93f2-f2d8cbbd09a2)
    
*   [Verification](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-21#id-0912d7a5-256e-4bf0-8f58-6b64932039a0)
    

Copy

    #PE1, PE2
    vrf def CUSTOMER
     add ipv4
      mdt default ingress-rep
      mdt auto-discovery ingress-rep
      mdt overlay use-bgp
    !
    router bgp 100
     add ipv4 mvpn
      neighbor 10.10.10.10 activate
    
    #P1
    router bgp 100
     add ipv4 mvpn
     neighbor-group IBGP
      add ipv4 mvpn
       route-reflector-client
    
    #PE3
    router bgp 100
     add ipv4 mvpn
     neighbor-group IBGP
      add ipv4 mvpn
       route-reflector-client
     vrf CUSTOMER
      add ipv4 mvpn
    !
    route-policy USE_IR_DEFAULT
     set core-tree ingress-replication-default
    end-policy
    !
    router pim vrf CUSTOMER add ipv4
     rpf top route-policy USE_IR_DEFAULT
     mdt c-multicast-routing bgp
    !
    multicast-routing add ipv4 int lo0 en
    multicast-routing vrf CUSTOMER add ipv4
     mdt so lo0
     mdt default ingress-rep
     bgp auto-discovery ingress-rep

# PIM Boundaries using MSDP | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-using-msdp.md)
.

Load **multicast.multi.domain.init.cfg**

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:multicast.multi.domain.init.cfg
     
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:multicast.multi.domain.init.cfg
    commit replace
    y

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FHP7ZIIcssdCoJOE2S0k6%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dc0843018-0528-45f6-895b-ed0d6c918938&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=3543967e8c5f0fe5a067e080c389f706&sv=3)

The group of routers circled on the left should be a PIM sub-domain. Traffic for multicast group 239.10.0.0/24 should not leak out this domain.

Configure R6 and R9 as anycast RPs using BSR. Use MSDP to prevent multicast traffic for 239.10.0.0/24 from leaking outside the sub-domain.

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-using-msdp#id-954c0906-8dfc-4d92-b80a-f90f64ca0969)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-using-msdp#c50b6cd4-a168-4897-8154-6d04c41d45eb)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Now that we are familiar with MSDP, we can revisit our “intra-IGP multi-domain PIM” problem. PIM domains, for ASM, are essentially bound by a group of routers sharing the same RP mapping information. In previous solutions, we attempted to block the propagation of RP information between our PIM sub domains. This prevents multicast traffic from working for certain group ranges between domains.

Now that we are familiar with MSDP, we can implement this functionality in a more elegant way. All RPs in the entire topology simply run Anycast RP. This provides HA for the RP. In addition, MSDP must be used for Anycast RP. We can filter which groups we send SA messages for, to enforce domain boundaries. Whatever groups an RP sends SA messages for become inter-domain multicast capable. Any groups the RP does _not_ send SA messages for bounds the multicast traffic to that local domain.

For this to work correctly, all routers in a subdomain must use a single RP. For this reason, we increase the cost of XR4’s links to the other domain, so that routers such as R7 use R6 as the closest Anycast RP node.

Next, besides implementing normal Anycast RP configuration, we just instruct R6 to only send SAs for groups other than the groups which must stay local to the subdomain.

On R2 and R4, we join groups 239.10.0.1 and 239.20.0.1:

Now R1 pings these groups. Traffic for 239.10.0.1 does not generate an SA on R6, due to the ACL associated with the **redistribute** command. R9 never learns of the (R1, 239.10.0.1) entry and R4 never receives the traffic:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FGm6F7VCe1r9F3KBd2ELS%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D8f50aa3a-4344-4617-8cd7-62e4d333a84e&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=d4ccbcde01ee9c4e3569da162920b6c8&sv=3)

R1 then pings 239.20.0.1. R6 _does_ send an SA for this (S, G) entry to R9. R9 is then able to join the (S, G), and R4 receives the traffic:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FqqPX1gzSulUWYzTgr0zD%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dcc07f12a-c920-4418-8f54-04254c6ba939&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=0f35b5f2ab685ed782a4d47852fb31cd&sv=3)

[PreviousInterdomain MBGP Policies](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/interdomain-mbgp-policies)
[NextMVPN](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn)

Last updated 1 year ago

*   [Answer](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-using-msdp#id-954c0906-8dfc-4d92-b80a-f90f64ca0969)
    
*   [Explanation](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-boundaries-using-msdp#c50b6cd4-a168-4897-8154-6d04c41d45eb)
    

Copy

    #R6, R9
    int Lo0
     ip pim sparse-mode
    int lo100
     ip add 1.0.0.100 255.255.255.255
     ip ospf 1 area 0
     ip pim sparse-mode
    !
    ip pim bsr-candidate lo0
    ip pim rp-candidate lo100
    
    #R6
    ip msdp peer 1.0.0.9 connect-source lo0
    ip msdp originator-id lo0
    ip msdp redistribute list REDIST_GROUPS
    !
    ip access-list ext REDIST_GROUPS
     deny ip any 239.10.0.0 0.0.0.255
     permit ip any any
    
    #R9
    ip msdp peer 1.0.0.6 connect-source lo0
    ip msdp originator-id lo0
    
    #XR4
    router ospf 1
     area 0
      interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0.524
       cost 100
      interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0.594
       cost 100

Copy

    #XR4
    router ospf 1
     area 0
      interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0.524
       cost 100
      interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0.594
       cost 100

Copy

    #R6
    ip msdp redistribute list REDIST_GROUPS
    !
    ip access-list ext REDIST_GROUPS
     deny ip any 239.10.0.0 0.0.0.255
     permit ip any any

Copy

    #R2
    ip multicast-routing dist
    !
    int gi2.525
     ip pim sparse-mode
     ip igmp join-group 239.10.0.1
     ip igmp join-group 239.20.0.1
    
    #R4
    ip multicast-routing dist
    !
    int GigabitEthernet2.543
     ip pim sparse-mode
     ip igmp join-group 239.10.0.1
     ip igmp join-group 239.20.0.1

# Start | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/vpws/start.md)
.

These labs were mostly inspired from Nick Russo's CCIE-SPv4 guide. Note that like usual, the CSR1000v interfaces have increased by one. (What was Gi1 in the original lab is now Gi2, etc). Outputs will still reflect the old Gi1 interface, but config solutions will reflect the correct Gi2 interface.

To begin, run the following command on your containerlab machine:

Copy

    cd ccie-spv5.1-labs/
    containerlab deploy -t l2vpn/l2vpn.clab.yml --reconfigure

Once all nodes are started, run the following command to transfer the config files to all nodes. These files will be used to change between startup configs for subsequent labs.

Copy

    python3 transfer_configs_to_nodes.py

The script will prompt you for a directory name. Enter "l2vpn".

Use the MTPutty session file located in **l2vpn/l2vpn\_putty\_sessions.xml** to quickly setup your SSH sessions to the nodes. Go to **Server - Import Tree** and browse for the file.

When you are done with the lab, use the following command to wipe it:

Copy

    containerlab destroy -t l2vpn/l2vpn.clab.yml

# SR LAN Adjacency SID (Walkthrough) | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/sr/sr-lan-adjacency-sid-walkthrough.md)
.

ISIS[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/sr/sr-lan-adjacency-sid-walkthrough#isis)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A LAN segment has been setup between R1, R2, and R3. R3 has been elected DIS.

Each router on the LAN advertises a **LAN-ADJ-SID**, one per node on the LAN. Each LAN-ADJ-SID sub TLV is attached to the Extended IS Reachability TLV which identifies the adjacency with the pseudonode.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FiVjG01tKrFxZ0hjtz1oE%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Da6f21a65-e905-4a4c-9d25-7d34f7558b13&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=6ecf41b23266137acdd2ae5d64f7f4ec&sv=3)

We can also see this using the same **show adjacency** command. As usual, both a FRR and non-FRR Adj-SID are allocated:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FVZnSZlz71HTC56lMSviE%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Ddc61a2d6-dfe7-447a-8e39-a95b078c123a&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=ef2ab47e259691c9cd84efe236bb4872&sv=3)

This allows SR to operate on a LAN somewhat as if the LAN was a collection of p2p links. This is because, on a LAN, the router only advertises an adjacency with the pseudonode. However, with SR, we have a LAN-ADJ-SID per node on the LAN.

The DIS does not advertise any SR information:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FroYASGfq6EAND1xWJUWO%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D6cc913df-5c7a-4e27-be3a-b8bd3774ce90&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=c655d5d5f02e48f4f440a44cc72f334f&sv=3)

Note that while a FRR-eligible Adj-SID is allocated, these are not TI-LFA protected.

OSPF[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/sr/sr-lan-adjacency-sid-walkthrough#id-2559adb8-7a23-41a3-aaaa-1bca12db8e0e)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The OSPF LAN-Adj-SID works slightly differently. Each node advertises a normal Adj-SID with the DR, but a LAN-Adj-SID with each BDR/DROTHER.

For example, R3 is the DR. R1 advertises a LAN Adj-SID for R2, and a regular Adj SID for R1:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FJ1jBDagu1Hk2AcUKIwaC%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D056d5d3b-667e-4a81-b4dd-27f102eaf72b&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=2d73076215b948bd81a155bd3e572659&sv=3)

The DR will have a LAN-Adj-SID with all nodes on the LAN:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FMZyH2Tl4OhtBU4KtmrnK%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D79e9828f-7f00-42ad-b92f-eda160df8606&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=228a53674e84988220717c35f11ef691&sv=3)

. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-duplicate-traffic-troubleshooting.md)
.

Load **pim.dup.traffic.tshoot.cfg** in the Russo SPv4 lab in EVE-NG.

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:pim.dup.traffic.tshoot.cfg
     
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:pim.dup.traffic.tshoot.cfg
    commit replace
    y

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FZOzb4gk0DfNJK7fd2pg4%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D3518d921-1f10-458d-ae4b-0e2d5396ccf7&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=fd2446997eb4baae8baabb4968eabf6e&sv=3)

R5 is connected to a LAN segment, with R10 and R6 as HSRP gateways. R5 has joined (\*, 239.1.2.3).

When R3 pings this group, R5 receives duplicate traffic. Explain the issue and find a way to fix it.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FOjDrHJ3e7geGtHVmT2IQ%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D46a1e08c-cbd8-4dd6-893e-d9e93228f3a3&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=5f00a1458674f090a5ef83b62e787972&sv=3)

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-duplicate-traffic-troubleshooting#id-3dc2729b-43cc-4bb7-bdce-cd12d4cd4b58)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-duplicate-traffic-troubleshooting#id-146d2217-f886-4c81-acc5-f39e2d5f3f2f)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Currently, R10 and R6 have **ip pim passive** set on the LAN interface. This can be used to prevent formation of a PIM adjacency on an interface facing receivers/senders, while still enable PIM functionality. However, when two routers connect to the LAN segment, each router will end up electing itself as PIM DR and create a distribution tree rooted at the source/RP.

On R10 and R6 we see that Gi2.100 is enabled in mode “passive” and each believes it is the DR.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FBf940NFsJS9iGSbCv7lZ%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D0aba2dab-e3d1-4c22-b156-4502281b7a32&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=5b80b719efb46a1aab10c530d32167b7&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FDLNNcitCZu6lICyqpEIq%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D12947e1c-8aaf-4d51-9435-1dfb18ef45e5&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=49499c38b75389396819cd27faaca6f0&sv=3)

Due to this, both routers build a (\*, G) rooted at the RP, which is XR4. On XR4 we see there are two outgoing interfaces in the OIL. One leading to R10 and one leading to R6.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FyohRVcUXAzGRnRbc4Srm%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dbbc185c5-257a-43f8-bd04-a40a6a2bb046&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=3c1d863a6914b0533a5c268a12813600&sv=3)

Once the traffic is seen, it switches over to a SPT. R6 branches this traffic out onto the LAN and to R10. Also notice above that gi2.100 is operating in sparse-dense mode when using **ip pim passive**.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FhEFMqVkz1tNzZYlQT8E4%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Db4420c1e-dd06-423b-ab1c-6a7ecd9a4a3a&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=f6e6f352c0f132528cb5915d26508007&sv=3)

Because the interfaces are running in PIM passive mode, no PIM assert is sent on the LAN. This would normally be used in PIM-DM to stop this duplicate traffic. Instead, we should run in normal PIM-SM mode where there are multiple routers on a receiver LAN.

The routers now elect a DR. R6 is elected for the highest IP.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252Fk0xdewfXiOcRZWyQtztB%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Db1a173ad-aa5a-4b93-89eb-721f3cb636e2&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=fd831c2381ce9ad2175021bc8e7c837f&sv=3)

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FVrnOBURkwZr8xJKKPnLu%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D42740f16-edee-4086-9569-ab1bb3f6d9cc&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=adf915bacfeeee46a04603ac3f7f6942&sv=3)

Now that R10 is no longer a DR, it prunes itself from the (\*, G) and (S, G) tree. R6 is the only router that should send PIM Joins on behalf of clients on the Gi2.100 LAN. The duplicate traffic is no longer seen.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F5IwLeEDTGIGDAIfUT6qi%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D235d80c1-6d02-4f11-a4c0-27c23c0e8274&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=b6bfd7948d28d48bd3524b18d22eb827&sv=3)

Note that this feature (**ip pim passive**) does not appear to be available on IOS-XR. This is likely because on IOS-XE, this runs the interface in sparse-dense mode, and sparse-dense mode isn’t supported on IOS-XR. Instead you can use a neighbor filter on IOS-XR and deny **any any**, but the PIM Assert process appears to still work in this case, so you wouldn’t see duplicate traffic on the LAN.

[NextUsing IOS-XR as a Sender/Receiver](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/using-ios-xr-as-a-sender-receiver)

Last updated 1 year ago

*   [Answer](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-duplicate-traffic-troubleshooting#id-3dc2729b-43cc-4bb7-bdce-cd12d4cd4b58)
    
*   [Explanation](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/multicast/pim-duplicate-traffic-troubleshooting#id-146d2217-f886-4c81-acc5-f39e2d5f3f2f)
    

Copy

    #R6, R10
    int gi2.100
     no ip pim passive
     ip pim sparse-mode

Copy

    #R6, R10
    int gi2.100
     no ip pim passive
     ip pim sparse-mode

# Profile 1 with data MDTs | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-1-with-data-mdts.md)
.

Load **basic.profile1.cfg**

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:basic.profile1.cfg
    Y
    
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:basic.profile1.cfg
    commit replace
    y

Configure the core so that customer multicast traffic is only delivered to PEs that have interested receivers. In other words, PEs that have (\*, G) or (S, G) state in the C-PIM for that group.

To verify, join a group on C2, and ping this from C1 with size 1400 and timeout 1. This will create a flow that exceeds 1kbps.

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-1-with-data-mdts#b03795e5-7cd5-4027-926c-67b2a9049be6)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Just like with profile 0, we can use data MDTs to create better efficiency when delivering customer multicast traffic across the core. The ingress PE advertises the group number it will switchover to inside the default MDT. PEs with interested receivers join a P2MP mLDP tree rooted at the ingress PE. The opaque value consists of the VPN ID plus a number that the ingress PE chose to represent this data MDT.

On the PEs, define the data MDT range:

Join 239.1.2.3 from both C1 and C3, and ping this group from C2.

PE2 will pick a MDT ID value (likely 1) and advertise this to the PEs. Both PE1 and PE3 will join the data MDT, which is a p2mp tree rooted at PE2. (As we saw on XRv data MDTs with profile 0, XRv will only join MDT data groups, not switchover to them as an ingress PE).

PE2 uses group number 1 for this (S, G) stream:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FWCeBjslAjcGoZnQZOPkd%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D11191f3b-20d9-4858-85fc-7ee74f8030f9&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=5d343fdd8120265e7c5dee4ec4b12569&sv=3)

PE1 joins it:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252Fp3hbyku73KRbuO54Ye6n%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D7bce5cfa-ab6e-47af-90d9-94b286f77667&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=e5e3145111345cbe9fa0a33c54092df5&sv=3)

PE3 joins it as well:

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FROputZb2jppo1VcZvG23%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dfae00ffb-6497-4643-8c9e-30a85da5bf19&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=352483b40656868e6617dccfd6839352&sv=3)

P2 has a p2mp tree rooted at PE2 with VPN ID 100:1 and group number 1. Upstream clients are PE2. Downstream clients are P1 and PE3.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252FnFL7z8D1eO4quHubX2Ia%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D999d24ab-39a2-4ae7-9d3a-4f8397e82cb0&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=f64e4f691d2d06aad34af7a16f6f1415&sv=3)

# Profile 13 w/ Configuration Knobs | CCIE SPv5.1 Labs

For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/llms.txt)
. This page is also available as [Markdown](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-13-w-configuration-knobs.md)
.

Load **basic.startup.config.with.cpim.cfg**

Copy

    #IOS-XE
    config replace flash:basic.startup.config.with.cpim.cfg
    Y
    
    #IOS-XR
    configure
    load bootflash:basic.startup.config.with.cpim.cfg
    commit replace
    y

The basic IP addresses, L3VPN, and C-PIM between the PEs and CEs is pre-configured.

*   Configure multicast VPN using mLDP in the core using a MP2MP default tree.
    
*   You cannot use PIM in the core.
    
*   CE1 is predefined as the RP in the C-PIM via BSR.
    
*   PEs cannot form C-PIM adjacencies between each other. Instead use BGP for the overlay.
    

Set the following configuration knobs:

*   Use S-PMSI P2MP tunnels for C-(S, G) flows, and immediately switchover to them
    
*   A C-S ingress PE should wait 60 seconds before pruning (S, G) state after the last type 7 route is removed
    
*   The RP’s ingress PE should wait 45 seconds before sending an RPT-bit (S, G) prune to the RP after receiving a type 5 route
    

See answer below (scroll down).

Answer[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-13-w-configuration-knobs#da7573e2-6971-4c12-9696-9e234e15f225)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-13-w-configuration-knobs#ecdd541e-2ee2-413f-8732-b4217e326b31)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This lab tests your understanding of a few configuration knobs. By default, the S-PMSI switchover waits a few seconds to allow PEs to join the data MDT. To configure the ingress PE to immediately switchover to the data MDT we can use the following keyword:

We can test this out by joining an SSM group on C3 and pinging this from C2. This removes the PIM register and switchover process with PIM-SM.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F66QXkOM7uNlOK3QPG8ia%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D24f0e713-99cd-459b-af40-66987370382a&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=f1d43cff4bbe1fb2761e1be5b815a286&sv=3)

We see no loss of traffic with this. This appears to be because PE2 signals the S-PMSI route simply upon the (S, G) state from PIM-SSM. So when traffic begins, PE2 immediately switches to the P2MP mLDP tree, which PE3 has already joined.

For PIM-SM this process results in several lost packets. This is because the S-PMSI route cannot be pre-signaled ahead of time. The PIM Register process takes place and SPT switchover takes place. C2 doesn’t advertise the type 3 route for several seconds. During this time, packets are flowing on the default MDT. However, PE3, due to the **immediate-switch** keyword on its own data MDT defintion, appears to reject these packets for arriving on the default MDT instead of a data MDT. I verified that if I remove the data mdt config on PE3, then there is no packet loss.

![](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3072390383-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FkUz2C3GqnZcWhoVL6jfk%252Fuploads%252F3K3pIgUrT9eqSmqPCdrQ%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D1be32ed8-9946-422b-bf6d-f774345e62f1&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=bb01a472131652dab3673359c052835b&sv=3)

Prune Delays[](https://ccie-sp.gitbook.io/ccie-spv5.1-labs/labs/mvpn/profile-13-w-configuration-knobs#a022966f-ddff-4855-9618-f59b1ccde02a)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Next we look at prune delays. By default, the PE connected to the RP will send a RPT-bit (S, G) prune towards the RP upon learning a type 5 SA route. We can delay this using the following command:

However, this doesn’t appear to work properly on IOS-XE. When a source goes active, PE1 still immediately sends a prune towards the RP. Perhaps this is because the RPT-bit (S, G) prune is happening as a result of (S, G) state being built on the PE, because the RP itself joins a (S, G) tree.

We can also set the source-tree prune delay. This controls how long a PE will wait before sending a (S, G) prune after a type 7 route is withdrawn.

We can test this by leaving an SSM group on C3 that is rooted at C2. PE2 should wait 60 seconds before sending a (S, G) Prune to CE2. However, I see that PE2 sends the prune immediately, so this also does not appear to be functional on CSR1000v.

If we do it the other way around, with C2 joining a SSM group rooted at C3, we see that IOS-XR also sends the Prune immediately to CE3.
